reason: This passage (1 Samuel 1) describes Hannah's personal distress over her inability to have children and her subsequent prayer to God. While Hannah does lament and weep about her individual circumstances, the text does not contain any complaints about Hebrew leaders or their governance. The narrative focuses on a family matter—Hannah's childlessness and her eventual conception of Samuel—and her interaction with the priest Eli. There is no indication of collective complaint from the Hebrew people against their leaders.
